title: Micro-recipes + Compatibility Adapter: docs for tokens, buttons, tables, charts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a concise, example-first docs section that: (1) surfaces small, copy-pastable micro-recipes for common tasks (theme tokens, responsive button sizing, table column patterns, chart color mapping), (2) documents an in-repo compatibility adapter (compat-shim) and codemod workflow for teams migrating from legacy tokens/components, and (3) captures do/don't examples and accessibility guardrails. The goal is to reduce migration friction for product teams and make safe defaults explicit in the docs site.
acceptance_criteria: Publish new docs page under /docs/micro-recipes with 8 micro-recipes: tokens aliasing, token fallback, small/medium/large button mapping, table row virtualization pattern, sticky column header example, chart color palette example, chart accessibility (aria) snippet, codemod usage example.
Add a short- lived compat-shim README in the monorepo that shows import aliases and runtime warnings, and link to it from the docs page.
Provide one automated codemod (js tool) in the repo and document: running it, previewing changes, and rolling back. Include a GitHub PR template for migration PRs.
Include at least 2 accessibility checks and a checklist for reviewers; UX/Accessibility sign-off recorded in comments.
Add migration notes that define deprecation windows and recommended rollout approach (canary -> team-wide), plus at least one example customer-facing migration note template for release notes.
Docs page reviewed by PM and Engineering and merged to main with a follow-up issue for telemetry to track usage of the compat-shim within 4 weeks.
decisions: Favor semantic token aliases over one-time color swaps to preserve theme intent across components.
Implement compat-shim as a temporary import-layer (index.js) that emits console warnings and maps legacy names to new tokens; responsibilities for removal will be timeboxed to 6 months.
Codemods will be implemented as a single Node script (jscodeshift) with a dry-run flag; we'll publish example outputs in the docs.
Chart docs will prioritize color-contrast and tooltip semantics rather than deep API surface; link to chart-engineering RFC for advanced migration.
Button sizing mapping will default to token-based paddings rather than fixed px to support variable font scaling and accessibility.
